findings.title: Integration teardown can exceed vitest's default 10 s hookTimeout under host contention. In apps/api/test/integration/access-derived-race.test.ts:73-79, afterAll runs three DDL statements (DROP TRIGGER on scoped_assignment, DROP FUNCTION, DROP TABLE), api.close() and dropScratchDatabase(). That helper (packages/db/test/global-setup.ts:116) has its OWN 10 s wait budget (timeoutMs ?? 10_000) for other backends to disconnect. vitest.config.ts:49 raises only testTimeout (30_000) for the integration project, and no hookTimeout is set anywhere, so the whole hook gets vitest's default 10 000 ms. One required full integration run failed this way in round 14.
findings.reproduction: Candidate sha256:dd747fe1...c559, full disposable clone at 985d0fa, Node v22.22.2, PostgreSQL 16.13 disposable cluster on 127.0.0.1:5491. The host was shared with two other reviewers' concurrent runs: 4 CPUs, load average ~10. Command: QA_PG_PORT=5491 tests/qa/support/with-pg.sh pnpm test:integration. Run 1: Tests 200 passed (200), but Test Files 1 failed | 18 passed, exit 1, 'FAIL apps/api/test/integration/access-derived-race.test.ts ... Error: Hook timed out in 10000ms' at :73:1 (afterAll). The whole run took 221.77 s (transform 14.08 s), and this file alone took 58.7 s. Runs 2 and 3 (Node 22) and a Node 24 run were each 19/19 files and 200/200 tests, exit 0, at 27.8 s / 29.5 s / 31.8 s, with this file at ~1 s. In isolation, 5 runs unloaded and 5 runs with 6 CPU-burn processes all passed (22-race-file-flake-probe.log), so it did not reproduce on demand. The root cause is not isolated beyond 'teardown exceeded 10 s on a ~8x slowed host'. The candidates are the DROP TRIGGER lock wait (it needs a ShareRowExclusive lock on scoped_assignment) and the dropScratchDatabase wait. Either way, the hook budget (10 s) is no larger than one of its own internal waits (10 s). The same pattern (afterAll with dropScratchDatabase, no hookTimeout) is in 6 integration files: access-derived-race, oidc, bootstrap, migrate, scratch-drop, a13-job-idempotency.
findings.expected: A required check is deterministic: a teardown that is allowed to wait up to 10 s internally runs under a hook budget comfortably larger than that, e.g. hookTimeout >= 30_000 in the integration project, matching testTimeout, or an explicit timeout argument on these afterAll hooks. On a slow or contended CI runner it should not turn a 200/200 run red.
findings.actual: The integration project inherits vitest's default hookTimeout of 10 000 ms. Under heavy host load, the afterAll of access-derived-race.test.ts timed out once in 3 full Node 22 runs, and the suite exited 1 although every test passed. No product behaviour is affected: all assertions passed. This is test-harness reliability in the F-DG1-009 area, a different mechanism from F-DG1-009 (that was concurrent files and an unhandled 57P01). Rated Low and non-mandatory: no data integrity, access-control, calculation or portability impact, and it needs severe host contention to trigger.
